| clean core | — | — | Yes | This names an initiative and concept that focuses on keeping an organization’s core ERP systems transparent, flexible, consistent, efficient, and cloud-compliant, so they can easily transition to the cloud. A clean core describes an up-to-date IT system with the latest releases, cloud-compliant extensions and integrations, with optimal primary data quality and process design. The core describes the main aspects of an ERP system, including extensibility, processes, data integration, and operation. Following a clean core strategy means reducing and process inconsistencies, establishing governance structures, maximize standard functionality, building cloud-compliant extensions which are integrate through stable interfaces, and minimizing complex customization. A clean core approach makes it easy for organizations to upgrade more cost-effectively and with lower potential risk.   This is not a priced offering but a way to convey what SAP hopes to provides for its customers.  You can add "ERP" to "clean core" (e.g., clean core ERP) to be more specific.  Note: this name should be kept in English and not be translated.   Do not abbreviate. Incorrect: CC. The name "clean core" appears in lowercase in normal text in all communications and marketing collateral except instances where title case is required, such as UI tiles. Do not add “SAP.” Incorrect: SAP clean core; SAP clean core | — |

| Joule Agents | — | — | Yes | Definition: This names an umbrella term used to refer to [Use Case] Agents. Agents are software systems that perform multi-step workflows using AI models to decide which actions to take and in which order and then interact with tools to execute their plans. Agents can reason, plan, and act to address a wide range of situations that would be impractical or impossible to automate with business rules or pre-configured logic. All agents delivered by SAP are Joule Agents. Agents developed using agent builder in Joule Studio by customers or third parties such as system integrators or consultants on behalf of an SAP customer should be referred to as “custom Joule Agents” at first mention. Thereafter, you can refer to them as “custom agents.” There are three types of Joule Agents, classified as conversational, embedded, or background, based on how the agent is designed to operate. The three types are further defined here: Conversational Joule Agents are experienced through a user’s conversational chat. They can be initiated by a user prompt or UI action, or they run in the background until triggered by another agent or system event, at which point they proactively engage a user in the Joule panel. Note: conversational agents also can be integrated with non-Joule conversational panels. • Example: Users interact with the Dispute Resolution Agent is activated by the user to automate analysis and resolution of common customer dispute cases. | — |

| SAP Cloud ERP | — | — | Yes | This name replaced SAP cloud ERP, May-2025.  This names a marketing handle for SAP’s cloud-based ERP applications and capabilities.  It's how we refer to SAP’s cloud-based ERP applications and capabilities as a whole and isn’t an individual product or package on the price list. While cloud ERP is traditionally associated with finance, supply chain management, and HR, we’ve aligned with Gartner’s expanded definition of ERP as “an integrated suite of business applications…covering broad and deep end-to-end processes like those found in finance, HR, distribution, manufacturing, services, and the supply chain.” “SAP Cloud ERP” is no longer the umbrella term for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, as it now refers to all cloud-based applications from SAP, not just public cloud applications. A descriptor is not required after SAP Cloud ERP. Add the descriptor “applications" or "capabilities" after “SAP Cloud ERP” to refer to all cloud-based ERP applications and capabilities across SAP. For example:  "With SAP Cloud ERP applications, you can run, build, and grow your business with industry best practices."  "With SAP Cloud ERP capabilities, you can run your company's core operations with confidence." Use "SAP Cloud ERP applications" to refer to cloud-based applications from SAP. It serves as a way to refer to applications as a whole and isn’t an individual product or solution you can buy on the price list. | — |

You can refer to this as:• SAP Cloud SDK for Java On GitHub only, where names appear in lowercase and hyphenated, you can refer to this as:• cloud-sdk-java Java is an object-oriented programming (OOP) language, while Java Script is an OOP scripting language. | — |

Base erosion and profit shifting refers to tax planning strategies that multinational enterprises use to exploit loopholes in tax rules to avoid paying taxes. | SAP Health Data Services for FHIR | — | — | Yes | This name fully replaced project “FHIR development framework,” Dec-2022.  This names a service layer for cloud applications that handles health-related data and dedicated applications designed for industries such as, e.g., healthcare, life sciences, public sector, or insurance. Running on SAP Business Technology Platform, it helps to develop healthcare applications that benefit from using the Health Level Seven (HL7) Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) standard. It supports the design, implementation, and operation of a native cloud application or services relying on health-related data. Its key capabilities include a REST API and messaging endpoint, FHIR profiling support, storing data in SAP HANA Cloud, and extensibility for resources, events, and business flows. At an early point in communication spell out “Health Level Seven” and “Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources.” Health Level Seven (HL7) International is a non-profit ANSI-accredited standards development organization dedicated to providing standards and solutions that empower global health data interoperability. Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR), pronounced “Fire,” is a standard describing data formats and elements and an application programming interface for exchanging electronic health records. The standard was created by the Health Level Seven International health-care standards organization. | — |

| SAP Key Management Service | — | — | Yes | The solution will be available Jan-2026. This names a service that provides simplified cryptographic key provisioning, control, and monitoring services to protect a customer's sensitive data. In a bulleted list or the pricelist, refer to it as: • SAP Key Management Service After first mention you can abbreviate the name as “SAP KMS.”   Do not precede with SAP BTP. Incorrect: SAP BTP Key Management Service   This offering works for cloud applications from SAP as well as for public clouds, including Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Amazon Web Services (AWS).   A key management service is an independent service that handles the management of cryptographic keys in a cryptosystem. This includes dealing with the generation, exchange, storage, use, crypto-shredding (destruction) and replacement of keys. It includes cryptographic protocol design, key servers, user procedures, and other relevant protocols. Do not confuse with SAP Data Custodian Key Management Service. SAP Key Management Service is for customers who want to protect their keys for all LoB solutions including SAP BTP with an easy and automatic setup. and will be available starting January 2026. SAP Data Custodian Key Management Service is for existing SAP S/4HANA  customers who bought the product in the past or need it before the official launch of the new product. | — |

| SAP Mode 2 Garage | — | — | Yes | This names an initiative and concept that gives customers an easy introduction and demo of SAP technology as well as a way to experience agile methodology with design thinking.  Initially a dedicated physical space in Switzerland, this is now a hybrid of both virtual and on-site. Mode 1 is optimized for areas that are more predictable and well-understood. It focuses on exploiting what is known, while renovating the legacy environment into a state that is fit for a digital world. Mode 2 is exploratory, experimenting to solve new problems and optimized for areas of uncertainty. These initiatives often begin with a hypothesis that is tested and adapted during a process involving short iterations, potentially adopting a minimum viable product (MVP) approach. Both modes are essential to create substantial value and drive significant organizational change, and neither is static. Do not alter the spelling of the name. Underlying offerings do not need to include “SAP Supply Chain” in names, but can if it helps simplify the name and clearly communicate what it does. Dos •	Do use the appropriate descriptor to clarify what you’re communicating, since SAP Supply Chain refers to all supply chain-related offerings, solutions, programs, tools, and content across SAP. | SAP Supply Chain Orchestration | — | — | Yes | This names an orchestration solution that uses N-tier (multi-tier) architecture insights to help COO, CIOs, and supply chain decision-makers mitigate supply chain disruptions. It unifies network risk and disruption sensing with transactional insights and AI capabilities to turn signals into coordinated, executable actions across systems and teams. Orchestration (in software) refers to the automated coordination of services and processes across systems to execute complex workflows, or achieve specific goals. N-tier (in this context) refers to multi-tier supply chain visibility, such as the ability to map and infer supplier relationships and disruptions across direct and indirect tiers (tier-1, tier-2, tier-N), typically enabled through advanced data models such as knowledge graphs. This enables customers to sense upstream risks (e.g., forced labor, geopolitical disruption) and orchestrate coordinated actions across the network. Do not omit SAP. Incorrect: Supply Chain Orchestration Do not abbreviate. Incorrect: SAP SCO | — |

| SAP Sustainability | — | — | Yes | This names a marketing handle comprising all sustainability products, solutions, services, programs, tools, and content from SAP and serves as a way to communicate sustainability capabilities across SAP’s lines of business.  You can add a descriptor like “solutions,” “portfolio,” or “offerings” after “SAP Sustainability” for clarity. Use the descriptor "portal" and “site” to refer to this access point. Do not capitalize “portal” or “site” except in titles, subtitles, headers, subheaders, UI tiles, or wherever title case is required. Do not refer to SAP Sustainability portal as IVY, IVY Portal, SAP IVY, or SAP IVY Portal. What is a marketing handle?  A marketing handle groups related offerings, often with diverse names, under a single and consistent name. The handle becomes a simple way of referring to the set as a whole, particularly when the offerings reside within separate portfolios or sub-brands. It simplifies marketing efforts by serving as the primary name in most communications but isn’t a single offering you can buy on a price list. How is this different from a sub-brand? | — |
